note: Selective JAK2 inhibitors (not ruxolitinib): fedratinib approved 2019 on JAKARTA spleen response with a Wernicke's encephalopathy boxed warning; NS-018 (ilginatinib) and BMS-911543 stopped after phase 1/2 for business reasons.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Cancer Cell, Europe PMC). Quote is the first 36 words of a longer sentence.
engagement.note: Fedratinib (TG101348) cut pSTAT5 and JAK2V617F disease burden in the mouse model; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Mouse: pSTAT5 and allele burden fall
engagement.quote: In vivo responses were correlated with surrogate endpoints, including reduction/elimination of JAK2V617F disease burden assessed by quantitative genomic PCR, suppression of endogenous erythroid colony formation, and in vivo inhibition of JAK-STAT signal transduction

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Human doses were set by phase 1 escalation (MTD 680 mg/d), not by a model-stated exposure target. NS-018 (2014) and BMS-911543 (2015) mouse papers likewise state none.
dose.judgement: The mouse's lack of toxicity is not a stated margin at a human-relevant exposure, so dose stays untested.
dose.note: Mouse efficacy at 60-120 mg/kg twice daily; no human exposure target or tolerability margin was stated from the model.
dose.quote: There were no apparent toxicities and no effect on T cell number.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA review NDA 212327 restates the mouse data (splenomegaly, fibrosis, survival).
efficacy.note: Fedratinib shrank extramedullary hematopoiesis (spleen) and attenuated fibrosis in JAK2V617F mice.
efficacy.quote: In treated animals, there was a statistically significant reduction in hematocrit and leukocyte count, a dose-dependent reduction/elimination of extramedullary hematopoiesis, and, at least in some instances, evidence for attenuation of myelofibrosis.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: spleen reduction: mouse extramedullary hematopoiesis vs patient SVR35 rate
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read; NCT01437787 results first posted 2026-08-11 per ClinicalTrials.gov. The FDA review (2019) relies on the same primary endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: JAKARTA reports no mouse data. The model is a PV-like V617F transplant model, scored for MF because it was the cited efficacy model in the FDA review. NS-018 (Nakaya 2014, same model type) also predicted spleen and fibrosis gains; phase 1 agreed (spleen 56%, fibrosis improved in 37%) but its primary endpoint was safety. BMS-911543 had 'limited activity' in this model (Pomicter 2015); NCT01236352 results (posted 2019-05-21) show 3 partial remissions in 42 phase II patients, and the program stopped for business reasons, so it is unsettled and not scored. NS-018 phase 2b NCT04854096 was terminated with 0 primary responders in either small arm (business decision), also unsettled.
efficacy.note: JAKARTA: 36-40% on fedratinib vs 1% on placebo reached the primary 35% spleen-volume reduction, as the mouse predicted.
efficacy.quote: The primary end point was achieved by 35 of 96 (36% [95% CI, 27%-46%]) and 39 of 97 (40% [95% CI, 30%-50%]) patients in the fedratinib 400-mg and 500-mg groups, vs 1 of 96

patient_trials.quote: By six and 12 cycles of treatment, 39% and 47% of patients, respectively, had achieved a spleen response per International Working Group criteria.
A ⩾50% reduction in palpable spleen size was achieved in 56% of patients (47% of patients with prior JAKi treatment), and improvements were observed in myelofibrosis-associated symptoms.

efficacy.quote: Thus, TG101348 may be an effective inhibitor of JAK2V617F+ MPDs in clinical trials.

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the IND opened October 2007, so the IND-enabling toxicology predates it; the data were public only in the 2019 review.
safety.note: Rat and dog repeat-dose studies named marrow, GI and liver as target organs; no CNS findings of note.
safety.quote: There were no clear drug-related CNS effects in rats; eye miosis and lack of pupillary responses were observed but were non-dose-dependent.

safety.note: Mouse studies reported no apparent toxicities for fedratinib.
safety.quote: There were no apparent toxicities and no effect on T cell number.

safety.magnitude_basis: red cell and platelet counts: unchanged in mice vs drug-related cytopenias in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Model side quote (Nakaya 2014): 'NS-018 reduced leukocytosis and splenomegaly, improved bone marrow fibrosis and prolonged survival without decreasing the erythrocyte or PLT count'. Registry date is NCT01423851 results posting.
safety.judgement: The NS-018 paper stated a named on-target sparing (no fall in erythrocytes or platelets) that patients contradicted; scored contra. Thrombocytopenia in MF patients is partly disease-related, but these were called drug-related. Fedratinib's 2011 grade 3-4 anemia/thrombocytopenia was not scored against Wernig, since the hematocrit fall was that model's efficacy readout and platelet data were not seen at abstract level.
safety.note: NS-018 mice kept red cell and platelet counts; in phase 1 patients thrombocytopenia (27%) and anemia (15%) were the commonest drug-related events.
safety.quote: The most common drug-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia (27%)/anemia (15%) for hematologic events, and dizziness (23%)/nausea (19%) for non-hematologic events.
safety.reason: Cytopenias the mouse said NS-018 spared

safety.magnitude_basis: CNS/thiamine-deficiency harm absent in animals, present in patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text read (bundle). JAKARTA (2015) first reported the WE cases; the clinical hold was November 2013. A post-hoc 28-day rat study found no thiamine change but reached only 0.3-fold human AUC, so it neither reproduces nor clears the signal.
safety.judgement: Scored as a harm the species could show (rats develop thiamine-deficiency encephalopathy), although fedratinib's causal role in thiamine depletion remains debated in the review. The anemia, thrombocytopenia, GI and liver-enzyme findings the toxicology predicted did appear in patients; one contra outranks them on the track.
safety.note: Patients developed encephalopathy including Wernicke's (boxed warning) that the rat and dog studies had not shown; predicted marrow and GI toxicity held.
safety.quote: Encephalopathy, including Wernicke’s encephalopathy (a life‐threatening illness caused by thiamine deficiency), occurred in 7/608 (1.2%) of patients who received 500 mg of fedratinib in clinical trials.
safety.reason: Encephalopathy not seen in rat or dog

safety.quote: In vitro studies indicate that fedratinib potently inhibits the carrier-mediated uptake and transcellular flux of thiamine in Caco-2 cells, suggesting that oral absorption of dietary thiamine is significantly compromised by fedratinib dosing.

safety.note: Assay found weak ThTr inhibition only at ~100-fold clinical Cmax, failing to reproduce the encephalopathy patients had.
safety.short: Assay missed thiamine harm post hoc
safety.quote: Fedratinib in vitro inhibition of ThTr1 and ThTr2 was 24.5% and 44.2%, respectively, at 300 μM (about 100‐fold the Cmax in patients at the recommended daily dose of 400 mg).
